rationale: brainz declares memory-verbs-v1-PARTIAL rather than claiming conformance, and this file is where the difference is published rather than implied. `bun run conformance` grades an observed run against the `deviations` list by exact-set equality in both directions: a non-passing case that is not declared is a regression, and a declared deviation that starts passing is a stale publication that must be deleted. OBSERVED. 23 cases: 8 pass, 12 fail, 3 skip. The 15 non-passing cases are listed below, each with the argument for it. WHAT UNBLOCKED IT. This file published `status: blocked` from 2026-08-13 because the pinned runner's SDK caps at MCP revision 2025-11-25 and this server answered `initialize` with 2026-07-28 without negotiating down, so the client aborted before `tools/list` and graded zero cases. `negotiateProtocolVersion` in src/mcp/envelope.ts now echoes a revision the client supports. The blocker is deleted rather than kept, because the incompatibility it describes no longer exists and a stale blocker is the same false artifact as a stale deviation. FOUR BUGS WERE FIXED RATHER THAN DECLARED, and saying which is the point of this file. An earlier version of this rationale said three and omitted the fourth — which was the one most exposed to the charge this file exists to answer, so its omission was the worst available. It is (4) below. (1) The envelope stamped `protocol_version` with the dated MCP wire revision, because one constant carried both that and the version of this server's own response body. Once revision negotiation landed, the field was false under both readings at once — a client that negotiated 2025-11-25 was told 2025-11-25 at `initialize` and handed "2026-07-28" in every envelope of that connection. Split into MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION and MEMORY_VERBS_VERSION. (2) Tool errors serialised the code inside a container — `{error: {code, message}}` — so every reader of the error vocabulary brainz deliberately adopted, this runner included, compared against `[object Object]` and could not branch on any refusal. Flattened. (3) `suggestion` was populated by exactly one handler in the whole surface, which left the recoverability argument the tool-surface design is built on unimplemented at the point where it pays off. Every refusal now carries a fix. None of the three was declared as a deviation, because a deviation declared to avoid fixing a real bug is the worst artifact this file could hold. TWO CASES PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON, and the exact-set grading cannot see it. `remember rejects missing provenance` and `remember rejects ISO-8601 duration ttl (P30D trap)` both send a `fact` parameter and expect `invalid_params`; brainz refuses them because `statement` is missing, which happens to carry the code the case asserts. Neither exercises provenance validation or ttl parsing, because brainz has neither. They are graded pass and correctly absent from the list below; this sentence is the only place that fact is recorded. TWO SHAPE MISMATCHES ARE LATENT IN THIS RUN AND WILL SURFACE LATER. All six `remember` calls were refused and the target serves no `put_page`, so this run executed against an effectively empty brain: `recall.results` and `entity.suggestions` both came back as empty arrays, and the validator only descends into array items that exist. Two divergences were therefore invisible. brainz returns `suggestions` as an array of strings where the protocol wants `{slug, title, create_safety}` objects; and `recall.results` items are `{id, title, text, source_type, created_at, untrusted}` where the protocol wants `{slug, title, evidence, create_safety, provenance}`. `entity miss returns found:false + suggestions` passes here ONLY because its suggestion list is empty. Neither is declared below: a deviation entry for a case the runner graded `pass` is a stale_deviation violation and would turn the gate red. They are recorded here as prose so that when a seeded corpus makes them fail, the next reader knows it is not a regression. SCOPE OF THIS MEASUREMENT. The entity-card hit path and the private-fact fence case were skipped for want of a seeding tool, and the live `synthesize` case was skipped by the runner's cost gate. This delta says nothing about any of the three. (4) `forget` answered `invalid_params` for an id this brain never issued, because `parseId` requires `kind:digits` and a bare integer parses as neither a known id nor a malformed one. It now answers `not_found` with a suggestion. Disclosed at length because it is the most contestable change in the wave and the one that most directly turns a case green: it reversed an explicitly-titled pin ('an unknown id is not_found and a malformed one is invalid_params') and changed a cross-surface contract asserted in test/mcp/equivalence.test.ts. The argument for it is that a caller cannot tell an id this brain forgot from one it never issued, and `invalid_params` tells them to fix their syntax when their syntax was fine. Whether that is a bug fix or a contract change, it belongs in this file either way, and it was not here.

deviations.reason: KTD3, argued economically rather than aesthetically in docs/research/2026-08-11-tool-surface-design.md. `synthesize` is the only verb whose marginal cost lands on the server instead of the caller, its cost scales with the user's corpus, and a model's judgement decides when to spend it — a shape gbrain has already paid for once (a recorded 53x overrun against estimate). The capability moved to the nightly consolidation cycle, where the spend can be estimated before it runs, capped mid-run, and amortised across every later `briefing` read. `synthesize` stays dispatchable-but-unadvertised and answers a typed `unavailable` pointing at `briefing`, so a caller carrying the frozen five gets an actionable refusal instead of `unknown_tool`. That research note states this consequence in as many words: brainz does not pass the certifier here, and publishes the difference.

brainz's `remember` takes one required `statement` and no `provenance`, `ttl`, `kind` or `visibility`; it answers `{id, status, page_id}` where the protocol wants `{id, status, entity_slug, valid_until}`. Renaming the parameter would flip nothing — schema validation would then fail on the three response fields brainz does not carry. NOT argued anywhere: an earlier version of this entry claimed each absent parameter was argued at its own site in src/mcp/tools/write.ts under the surface's parameter budget. Neither half is true — write.ts argues the absence of `origin` and constrains `source_type` and `media_type`, and says nothing about `provenance`, `ttl`, `kind` or `visibility`; and the budget does not bind, since MAX_PARAMS is 8 and `remember` declares four. So this is an unbuilt capability, not a declined one, and by this file's own rule a deviation nobody justified is a bug nobody noticed. It is published as unbuilt. What remains true is the hazard src/mcp/tools/index.ts names: accepting gbrain's parameters while ignoring them would be a declared parameter the handler ignores — a silently wrong answer wearing a certificate — so the fix is to build them or to keep saying plainly that they do not exist. NOT claimed as an isolation invariant: R15 governs `origin_context`, which is credential-derived and a different field from gbrain's free-text `provenance`, so R15 does not forbid brainz from accepting one. This deviation rests on nothing but the absence of the capability, which is what it now says. Filed while publishing this: docs/research/2026-08-11-tool-surface-design.md still describes `remember` with provenance mandatory, which the implementation does not do — the code is current intent and the doc is stale, and that needs ratifying rather than discovering here.

deviations.case: recall by entity round-trips the remembered fact (superset envelope)
deviations.reason: gbrain's `recall` publishes two lanes — consolidated `facts[]` plus a `results[]` search arm. brainz publishes one. Its ranked read fuses on chunk ids (`kind: 'chunk'` is hardcoded on every projected result); facts participate as ranking evidence through the relational arm and resolve back to the passages they came from, and are never returned as records. Adding a `facts` key would not flip these cases anyway: the `results` item schema diverges too (see the latent-findings note in `rationale`). These are two different response contracts, not one dropped field. The budget cases carry a second, independent reason: `recall with budget smaller than the first item drops everything` demands `total: 0`, and src/core/search/budget.ts states the opposite exception explicitly and on purpose — a single result larger than the entire budget is returned anyway, because returning nothing to a question the stack did retrieve an answer for is the worse failure. Passing that case means reversing an argued, tested decision. `budget_tokens`/`budget_used`/`dropped_count` echoes are cheap and worth adding on brainz's own terms; they are additive envelope growth, not a conformance obligation, and are not being added to satisfy a certifier.

deviations.case: entity resolves the round-trip entity to a card
deviations.reason: The runner seeds its conformance entity with `put_page` and skips these cases when the target has none. brainz serves no `put_page`: pages are written by connectors and by the write path behind `remember`, never by a caller choosing a slug and a body. That is a surface deviation in its own right rather than a gap — a tool that let a model author a page at an address it picked would be a model choosing which fence its writes sit behind — and it is declared here because a skip is a non-pass case and this file grades every one of them. Consequence worth stating: neither the entity-card hit path nor the private-fact fence case is exercised by this run, so this delta says nothing about either.

Two things, and only the second is a deviation. The immediate cause is a cascade from the `remember` deviation above: the id these cases retract is captured from a `remember` that was refused, so the literal placeholder string reached `forget` and was answered `not_found`. Underneath that, the response contract still differs: brainz's `forget` returns `{id, deleted_at, recoverable_until, cascade}` — retract-with-72h-recovery, with a cascade whose blast radius depends on what kind of record was retracted — where gbrain requires `{id, expired, reason}`. `expired: true/false` is a different model of the same verb. The id grammar itself round-trips correctly and is not at issue: `remember` returns `fact:<digits>` and `parseId` accepts exactly that, and the protocol says ids are opaque.

deviations.case: synthesize answers (or reports unavailable) — cost-gated, pass --synthesize
deviations.reason: Skipped by the runner's own cost gate, not by brainz: the case makes a live model call and only runs with `--synthesize`. Declared because a skip is a non-pass case and this file grades the exact set. It would fail if it ran, for the reason the two `synthesize` list cases above give — that is a prediction, and it is recorded as prose here rather than as a second entry.
